import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Hypothesis H

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schinzel%27s_hypothesis_H)
-/
open Polynomial
namespace Schinzel

/--
**Schinzel conjecture (H hypothesis)**
If a finite set of polynomials $f_i$ satisfies both Schinzel and Bunyakovsky conditions,
there exist infinitely many natural numbers $n$ such that $f_i(n)$ are primes for all $i$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem schinzel_conjecture (fs : Finset ℤ[X]) (hfs : ∀ f ∈ fs, BunyakovskyCondition f)
    (hfs' : SchinzelCondition fs) : Infinite {n : ℕ | ∀ f ∈ fs, (f.eval (n : ℤ)).natAbs.Prime} := by
  sorry

end Schinzel

reformulations.difference: Lean uses natural-number inputs, including zero, and primality of the absolute values, whereas the source asks for positive inputs and positive prime values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every polynomial satisfying BunyakovskyCondition has positive leading coefficient and positive degree, so its values are eventually positive. Since fs is finite, there is a common threshold beyond which every evaluation is positive. Beyond that threshold, absolute-value primality is exactly positive primality. Removing the finite initial segment, including zero, preserves infinitude. This equivalence is proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as SchinzelReview.infinite_abs_iff_positive_primes.

reformulations.difference: The source gives a disjunction: infinitely many simultaneous prime values, or a fixed divisor greater than one of the product. Lean instead assumes SchinzelCondition and concludes infinitude.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The source explicitly gives the equivalent obstruction of a fixed prime dividing every product value. A prime divides a finite product exactly when it divides some factor. Integer inputs can be replaced by nonnegative residue representatives modulo that prime, since integer-polynomial evaluations preserve congruences. Consequently SchinzelCondition is precisely the negation of this obstruction. Classically, (¬B → A) is equivalent to A ∨ B. The complete equivalence with the source's prime-obstruction formulation is proved as SchinzelReview.theorem_statement_equiv_wikipedia in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Checked the sole theorem and both imported custom conditions. Scratch proofs compile without sorryAx and do not invoke the conjecture. Boundary tests cover the empty family, zero and constant polynomials, negative leading coefficients, admissible examples X and X²+1, and the simultaneous obstruction for {X, X+1}. The research-open tag agrees with the source; the linked average-case result does not settle the universal conjecture.
